answer: Residency across distinct network islands is one workable barrier. Every epoch a beacon passes through a random prism of vantage points, and each operator is measured from all of them. Keys answering from one subnet, one datacentre, or one latency curve merge into a single cluster and count once between them. Holding ten thousand separate votes then means renting space in ten thousand separate networks, paying ten thousand providers monthly, while the schedule spirals outward and no operator knows where the next measurement lands. Fake geography is billed as rent in every island it claims.
